items.title: Host (non-device) tensors crash the process with SIGSEGV in ttnn.exp (all unary ops), where, concat/stack, split, tilize/untilize, repeat_interleave and clone instead of raising
items.evidence: ### Describe the bug Most ops raise a `RuntimeError` for a host tensor, for example `add`, `sum`, `transpose`, `matmul`, `softmax` and `gather`. These ops instead dereference `tensor.device()`, which is null for host storage, before any validation, and Python dies with a segfault. A common way to hit this is forgetting `device=` in `ttnn.from_torch`. ```python t = ttnn.from_torch(torch.randn(1, 1, 32, 32), layout=ttnn.TILE_LAYOUT) # no device= ttnn.concat([t, t], dim=-1) # Signal: Segmentation fault (11) in can_use_tiled_unaligned_concat ``` ##

items.title: [Low] A partial takeover that leaves the source between the liquidation and conservative price clears its observation and strands the remaining commitment as ineligible and unrepairable
items.evidence: A takeover is admitted when the source is unhealthy at the **liquidation** price, but the repair target is the commitment the source supports at the **conservative** price. A takeover whose `requested` amount is smaller than the full repair can move the source's max healthy price to at or above the liquidation price while it is still below the conservative price. `_clearHealthyLiquidation` then clears the source's adverse observation, so nobody can continue the repair — yet the whole remaining position is still excluded from healthy commitment.

items.title: [Bug bounty] SDK (PAPI): sends funds to a different account when a 0x recipient has the wrong length
items.evidence: # 🐞 Bug Report ## 🔍 Describe the Bug On a non-EVM destination, `@paraspell/sdk` (PAPI) accepts a `0x` recipient of any length. items.evidence: # 🐞 Bug Report ## 🔍 Describe the Bug In XCM API 14.5.3, a caller with a valid API key and a successful reCAPTCHA can put a comma-separated address list in the higher-limit form's `email` field. items.title: `core/state`: BAL does not net same-index changes across multiple post-execution commits (EIP-7928)
items.evidence: ## Summary Geth rejects two EEST Amsterdam blocks that the execution-specs reference accepts, with `access list hash mismatch`. The cause is in post-execution BAL construction: when two system calls at the same block access index write the same value and their combined effect nets to the value at the start of the index, Geth still records a change. EIP-7928 requires that change to be demoted to a read (storage) / dropped (balance, nonce, code). This is a genuine spec violation, but it is **not reachable on mainnet** with the real predeploy code

items.title: [Medium] Pending sends never expire, have no cap, and cost ~nothing — permanent state bloat via reclaimable dust
items.evidence: ### Summary A pending send, once admitted, lives **forever** in every node's state. There is no expiry/TTL/pruning, no per-account or global cap on pending sends, and the minimum send amount is 1 micro-XE (the only check in `validateAndAddSend` is `amount == 0`). Creating a pending costs one 32-bit PoW solve (~2^25 hashes at the live difficulty) plus 1 micro-XE locked in the pending — and that micro is **fully reclaimable**, because the attacker names their own second account as destination and receives it back. items.title: Bounties: named topics an agent can be primed on in one call
items.evidence: ### Problem Memory is grouped under scopes that are bare ids with counts. Journal entries have no scope. An agent that has to continue another agent's work on a topic has no single way to load that topic: it must guess a scope id, run several recalls and search an unscoped journal. ### Outcome A user names a topic in conversation. Any agent on any client finds it, loads it in one call and continues the work. Topics never open or close; they accumulate knowledge and are updated as things change. "Bounty" is the product word for such a topic. ###

The demo vault's bug, a missing access check, is one call deep, so any bot that simulates calls finds it. A demo bounty whose funds a bot takes first can't be won by the AI agent, so the mainnet demo (ADR-0018: one bounty, won by an AI agent with a claim key) can't happen with that vault.

The key is released only to a guest whose attestation names the exact workload. The plaintext then exists only inside the VM. items.title: [RegisterSec] Anthropic won't fix a Claude Dispatch flaw that could let attackers execute remote commands across corporate boundaries
items.evidence: A vulnerability in Anthropic’s Claude products lets any browser extension that can control Claude Dispatch make Claude Desktop run code on the computer – or even a different machine signed into the same Claude account – with no browser exploit and minimal user interaction required. Anthropic, aware of the problem since May, has taken no action to close the hole. items.title: [intake 输入][缺陷复现] 承接 dsh-memory #762：注入面按 UTF-16 截断，半个 emoji 让整条会话永久 400
items.evidence: ## 承接 本仓只作进料登记，**技术正文、全部定位过程与读数在 [FuRongJun-1999/dsh-memory#762](https://github.com/FuRongJun-1999/dsh-memory/issues/762)**（2026-11-04 提）。不重复贴全文，避免与本仓既有条目重复计数。 ## 一句话 记忆注入按 UTF-16 码元截断，半个 emoji 变成孤立高位代理 `\uD83D`，写进对话历史后每个请求都被服务端以 400 拒掉；历史只增不改，会话永久作废。 ## 现象 `DeepSeek Messages request failed (400) INVALID_REQUEST`，3–8 秒返回、**0 token**、重发必现；同账号同模型新建会话完全正常。判据：400 + 秒回 + 0 token + 必现 ⇒ 请求体非法。 ## 根因 `lib/hooks.js:378`（main `src/hooks.ts:452`）用 `safe.slice(0, budget) + '…'` 按 UTF-16 码元截断，`'😊'.slice(0,1)` 得到 `'\uD83D'`；`JSON.stringify` 写成 `"\ud83d"`——
